turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hi, Neha. Come on in.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can I have your full name and date of birth,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: please? Neha Kolkarni, January 25th, 1987. Thanks.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How did your daughter's soccer tournament go?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: They lost in the semi -final, but Anaya scored, so she was over the moon. That's great.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So how's the mood been?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Good, actually. The Bopropian is still working. But um, there's something I wanted to bring up.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: My husband Vikram thinks I should talk to you about my drinking. I'm glad you did, tell me what it looks like.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Since I started working from home last year, a glass of wine at six turned into three, sometimes four most nights. Saturdays it can be five or six.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you often end up drinking more than you planned?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Pretty much always, I tell myself one glass. Have you tried to cut back?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: In August I tried to stop for a month, I made it four days. Do you ever drink in the morning or get shaky or sweaty when you go without?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, never in the morning and no shakes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any blackouts where you can't remember part of the night?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Once at a wedding in August I don't remember the end of the night. That kind of scared me.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any driving after drinking?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, never. I'm really careful about that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any smoking, cannabis, other drugs?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, none of that. What?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anyone in your family with alcohol problems.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My dad was a heavy drinker. He died of cirrhosis when I was in college.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm sorry, that's a lot to carry, and you're still on Bapropian XL, 150 milligrams every morning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, every morning.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I have to ask, any thoughts of suicide or of hurting yourself?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, not at all.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good, so your audit C score today is 8 out of 12. For women, three or more is a positive screen, so this is clearly in the risky range. Your pH Q9 is 4, so your depression is still in remission. Your blood pressure is a bit high today at 138 over 88, pulse 90. I don't see any tremor in your hands. You seem calm and open, your mood is good, and your thinking is clear.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, honestly, I figured it would be high. So here's where I land.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I think this is a mild alcohol use disorder. Your recurrent major depression is in full remission on the bupropion, and I want to it that way because alcohol can bring depression back. There's one more important thing. Bapropion lowers the seizure threshold, and heavy drinking, or stopping suddenly after heavy drinking, raises that risk.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Wow, I didn't know that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So what I'd like to do is this. First, a liver panel and a GGT at the lab on your way out. If those are okay, I'll start Naltric Zone 50 mg once a day. It cuts cravings and makes drinking less rewarding. I'll call you with the results before you start it. Okay, is it the same number on file?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 919 -555 -0117 That's what I have.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Second, a goal for now. No more than one drink a day and at least three alcohol -free days a week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Third,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm referring you to the Riverbend Recovery Center outpatient program. They have evening groups twice a week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Evening's work. Vikram can handle the kids.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep the bupropian at 150. If you get shaky, sweaty, or anxious when you cut down, call us right away. and if your mood drops or you have any thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text 988. We'll recheck your blood pressure next time. Let's meet again in four weeks on October 30th.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you. This is easier to say out loud than I thought.
